messages:
Sam K.: Hey team — urgent but short. I need to step out at 21:15 PST (around 2025-03-25T05:15Z). There's an ongoing Embeddings API error-rate spike (incident-bot pinged earlier). Can someone take primary for the next ~6 hours? I can stay on standby via phone for escalation but can't be the active primary.

incident-bot: PAGER: embeddings.prod / 5xx-rate spiking above 4% for 20m. Affected region: us-west-2. Incident page: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2025-0423 (severity: P2).

Priya R.: I can take primary until 03:30Z. I'll be at my laptop for the handover now. Jon, can you be secondary?

Jon M.: Yep I can be secondary. I'll shadow for the next 45m and then be available on pager. Taking note of current mitigations in the incident page.

Sam K.: Thanks. Quick notes from my side before I hand off: observed 500s are concentrated around the embeddings POST /v1/embeddings route, median latency normal but error-rate up; autoscaler is healthy. No config deploys in the last 2 hours. Customer impact limited to ~12% of embed requests failing (mostly retries causing UX errors). Runbook is here: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/embeddings-errors.

Priya R.: Copy. Two action items I will run immediately: 1) Check model fallback policy, 2) confirm kv-cache health & redis metrics. If errors persist, fall back traffic to quantized-embed-v1.

Sam K.: Exactly. Quick commands for triage (paste into your shell):

```bash
# check prod logs for 5xx spikes in embeddings service
kubectl logs -l app=embeddings --since=30m | grep "5.." | wc -l
# check redis errors
kubectl exec -it svc/redis-main -- redis-cli info | egrep "keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses|used_memory"
```

Jon M.: Ran the logs command during shadowing — error stack shows transient downstream 502 from the ffwd-cache (internal proxy). I’ll keep an eye on proxy timeouts.

Priya R.: I'm toggling the model routing policy to prefer quantized-embed-v1 for new requests as a canary (5% -> 25%). Doing a gradual ramp: 5 -> 25% now. Please don't escalate unless errors worsen.

incident-bot: ROUTING CHANGE: model routing updated for client-group=public to prefer quantized-embed-v1 at 5% -> 25%. Change initiated by Priya R. (audit id: rc-8492).

Emma L.: FYI ops SIG, this might require a short cache-warmup. Keep an eye on token-economy dashboards — cost per embed will jump slightly with fallback.

Sam K.: Priya — when you take the primary, please update the rotation calendar and runbook pinned note stating 'Sam out 21:15 PST -> Priya primary until 03:30Z' so SRE knows. Also mark the incident page with handoff note.

Priya R.: Done — calendar updated and incident page annotated with: "Primary switched: Sam -> Priya at 21:10 PST. Secondary: Jon."

Jon M.: Confirmed. I added a quick triage pointer in the incident page about ffwd-cache 502s. If the proxy continues to fail, escalation path is: 1) add a short 1s timeout in proxy route, 2) roll traffic to fallback pool, 3) open a ticket with infra-team for ffwd-cache.

Sam K.: One more: if customer-impact crosses 20% failing, page infra oncall and set severity to P1. Otherwise keep P2 and continue mitigations.

Priya R.: Copy. I'll also annotate the runbook with the temporary mitigation steps I just took.

Jon M.: Quick health check command to share with whoever is primary later:

`curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings/health -d '{"check":"kv,proxy"}' | jq .`

Priya R.: I'm on primary now. If anything critical happens ping my mobile or DM. Leaving a sticky note in the incident page with commands and the next-check times (every 10m for the next hour).

Sam K.: Appreciate it. I'm leaving now. Good handoff everyone. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: HANDOFF: user=Priya R. assumed primary for oncall rotation (start=1749009999, expected_end=1749035400). Audit log updated.

Priya R.: (post-handoff) Status at 21:30 PST: error-rate down to 2.1% after routing tweak. Continuing monitoring. If it holds under 3% for 30m we'll retire aggressive mitigations.

Jon M.: Shadowing until 22:00 PST then going to secondary-only. Noted about cache warmup.

Emma L.: Thanks team. Please add any lessons to the post-incident notes — particularly around routing-policy fallbacks and proxy timeouts.

Priya R.: Will do. I'll add a quick post-incident checklist before morning handback.
